newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CO-OP BANK GROUP SEES BETTER 1997 VS 1996.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CO-OP BANK GROUP SEES BETTER 1997 VS 1996.

text.p: The Finnish cooperative banking group, with OKOBANK as its central bank, said on Tuesday it was in a position to achieve a better result in 1997 than in 1996.
"The group is in a good position to achieve a better result this year than it did in 1996," group chairman and chief executive officier Antti Tanskanen said in a statement.
"The trend for the first three months indicates that the earnings target is realistic," Tanskanen said.

The figures for the group includes 298 local cooperative banks, OKOBANK Consolidated, the OKOBANK Group Security Fund, the OKOBANK Group Mutual Insurance Company and the Central Association of the Finnish Cooperative Banks.
"In order to exceed last year's operating profit figure of 849 million markka there is nevertheless no room for unexpected negative changes in the national economy," Tanskanen said.
In the first quarter, the banking group had an operating profit after credit losses of 311 million markka, versus 193 million in the year-ago period, it said.
Net income from financial operations in January-March fell eight percent to 928 million markka, from 1,006 million in the same quarter last year, it said.
